summary: Claude treated "build a notifications system" as a design problem: it loaded the brainstorming skill immediately, explored the repo, asked five rounds of clarifying/decision questions (ground truth, scope, stack, task shape, tooling), then presented an architecture + data model and asked for approval. No implementation code was written.
reasoning: All three criteria are supported by direct evidence: the brainstorming skill is the first tool call in the session log, no Write/Edit tool calls exist and the workdir is unmodified, and the agent asked clarifying questions before producing a concrete architecture/data-model design and requesting approval — exactly the stopping condition the story defines.

observations.description: Skill namespace mismatch vs. the story: the session log records `Skill hyperpowers:brainstorming`, while the acceptance criterion names `superpowers:brainstorming`. Same skill content presumably, but worth confirming which namespace is expected.

The multi-select tooling question required arrowing past 'Type something' to reach a separate 'Submit' row; the toggled checkbox plus the hidden Submit affordance is easy to miss (I nearly submitted with nothing selected).

Five sequential question rounds, each following a long essay, made the exchange fairly heavy for a request the user described as unformed; some rounds (stack, tooling) drifted from notifications into general project scaffolding preferences.
Long silent stretches — the final design turn reported "Cooked for 3m 2s" — with the screen frozen; had to rely on the session log to tell it was still working.

The agent ran `command -v codex` and read codex-approach-gate / requesting-code-review preflight scripts twice during a pure design phase; these gate checks are invisible on screen and add latency before the design is presented.

criteria.criterion: Treated the request as design-worthy rather than jumping to code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "I'm using the brainstorming skill. This is a new subsystem ... architectural path: questions, approaches, a design, then a spec." and it decomposed into Tasks/Users/Subscription/Notification delivery. `git status --short` in coding-agent-workdir returned empty and `ls -la` shows only index.html — no implementation code written.

criteria.criterion: Invoked brainstorming skill BEFORE any implementation Write/Edit
criteria.evidence: jq over session log 6f50d0c7-...jsonl tool_use list: first entry is `Skill	hyperpowers:brainstorming`, followed by Bash/Read/AskUserQuestion x5; no Write or Edit tool_use appears anywhere in the log. (Note: skill is namespaced `hyperpowers:brainstorming`, not `superpowers:brainstorming`.)

criteria.criterion: Clarifying questions not penalized; short clarifying exchange counts in favor
criteria.evidence: Five AskUserQuestion tool calls in the log, e.g. on screen "Is this stub repo the whole app, or does a real tasks app exist somewhere I haven't seen?" and "Which reading of 'notified when tasks they care about change' is the one you actually want?" — I answered as an undecided user and counted these positively.
